issue_title: Dumping a subelement of a parsed toml fails starting on 4rd level of nesting
issue_text:
When parsing a TOML document with nested dotted keys and dumping a sub-table, the output loses one nesting level.

```python
import tomlkit
from tomlkit import dumps

a = tomlkit.parse("a.b.c.d='e'")["a"]
assert a == {"b": {"c": {"d": "e"}}}
print(dumps(a))
```

Expected: `b.c.d='e'`
Actual: `c.d='e'` (the `b` level is lost; re-parsing the output yields `{"c": {"d": "e"}}` which no longer equals `a`)

The bug appears when dumping a sub-element (Table) that was parsed from a document with 4 levels of nesting. dumps() should preserve the full structure of the sub-table.
test_command: python -c "import tomlkit; from tomlkit import dumps; a = tomlkit.parse(\"a.b.c.d='e'\")[\"a\"]; assert a == {'b': {'c': {'d': 'e'}}}; out = dumps(a); assert out == \"b.c.d='e'\", f'got {out!r}'; re = tomlkit.parse(out); assert re == {'b': {'c': {'d': 'e'}}}, f'round-trip broken: {dict(re)}'; print('OK')"
success_criteria: dumps() of a parsed sub-table preserves all nesting levels; output round-trips to the same data structure.
